title: Per-row "Start this check now" is a silent no-op on the only state it is offered from (existing queued rows): 200 started:true, nothing created, no send, no re-arm
evidence: handle_start with ?slot= calls run_create_checks_slot, whose only write is insert_reference_call_if_absent (ON CONFLICT ... DO NOTHING against the live-slot index). The panel offers RefcheckStart only for status Queued, and a queued row IS a live row occupying the slot — so the insert always conflicts, returns 0 rows, and the handler responds {"started": true} (trigger.gleam:496) regardless of whether anything was created. The sweep (sweep_due_reference_calls.sql:54) is what actually sends, at its 15-minute cadence (reference-checks-job.tf / scheduler.tf). No re-arm of next_attempt_at, no queued->contact_initiated transition, no send from the start action.
detail: UX §7.4 wireframe promises 'Start this check now -> sends the invite now' and 'The row then moves to Invitation sent'; the AC's premise ('Given a queued row') guarantees the row exists, so the conflict path is the ONLY reachable case from the panel. The action accomplishes nothing the sweep wasn't already going to do, and its success toast ("Reference started — the invite goes out now.") is false in the very scenario the manual start exists for: a backed-up or down sweep. per_slot_start_creates_only_the_requested_slot_test only covers the no-row case, not the AC's premise. The ?slot= start on an already-started slot is an unhandled path: it returns success with no effect and no way for the client to distinguish (action_result_decoder reads only the optional reference_call_id, which the start response never carries).
recommended_fix: Make the per-row start re-arm an existing queued row (e.g. next_attempt_at = now() via a guarded UPDATE queued row -> immediate sweep eligibility, or an explicit send-now step), or return a distinguishable no-op response and suppress the success toast. At minimum, pin the already-started-slot behavior with a test.

title: Failed or hung correct/substitute/start/take-over requests leave the row's action controls permanently disabled with no in-session recovery
location: client/src/client.gleam:3537-3547 (ApiReturnedRefcheckAction Error branch), 6687-6730 (save_refcheck_edit), 3447-3466 (UserEditedRefcheckTrio), 6570-6643 (refetch/fire helpers); client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:994 (disabled: saving binding); client/src/model.gleam:374 ('All reset on route change' comment)
evidence: On Error, ApiReturnedRefcheckAction clears only refcheck_action_inflight; refcheck_edit is untouched, so its `saving: True` (set in save_refcheck_edit) persists and view_edit_trio renders the Save button disabled (reference_panel.gleam:994) forever — UserEditedRefcheckTrio resets only error, never saving, and no timeout effect exists (unlike the report-download flow's 90s download_timeout precedent). The code comment 'the landlord can retry' and refcheck_action_failure_toasts_error_test (which asserts the surfaces are kept) are both contradicted: the only recovery is Cancel + retype, losing the typed trio. Separately, refcheck_action_inflight has no timeout and is NOT reset on route change (BrowserChangedUrl's ApplicationDetail block resets refcheck_expanded/explainer_open only; the model.gleam:374 'reset on route change' comment is false) — a request whose response never settles (hung connection; browser fetch has no default timeout) leaves the call_id in inflight for the whole session, and every subsequent render of the start/take-over confirms for that row is disabled (busy = set.contains(inflight, call_id)).
detail: Two unhandled error paths in the new control surface: (a) a 4xx/5xx on save leaves saving=True with the Save button disabled, so the promised retry is impossible; (b) a never-settling request permanently disables that row's confirms (and its stale state survives navigation between applicants). Both recover only on a full page reload.
recommended_fix: Reset `saving: False` (and keep the edit open) in the ApiReturnedRefcheckAction Error branch, and add an unstick mechanism for refcheck_action_inflight (a timeout effect like download_timeout, or a route-change reset as the model comment claims).

title: Em-dashes in 5 new implementer-authored toast constants and the attempt-log export text violate the RT-wide em-dash ban (no_em_dash_test does not scan refcheck copy)
evidence: copy.gleam:874 'Reference started — the invite goes out now.'; 878 'Reference re-enabled — it's back in the queue.'; 880 'You're handling this one — automated messages stopped.'; 882 'Details saved — the invitation is on its way again.'; 884 'Referee substituted — the new invitation is on its way.'; client.gleam:6777-6780 joins attempt.at/channel/outcome with ' — '. Grep of the UX spec finds none of these phrases — they are implementer-authored, not spec-verbatim. The server-side reference_checks code documents the ban as RT-wide ('\u{2014} never') with tests asserting absence (messages_test.gleam:313, form_copy_test.gleam:174), and the client ban exists but only scans copy.toast/copy.page error copy (client/test/copy_test.gleam:308 no_em_dash_test) — the known pin gap from RC4.2 r2's carried warning, into which this PR adds six more instances (the carried finding's same-defect clause applies).
detail: User-facing landlord copy with em-dashes ships despite the RT-wide ban; the no_em_dash_test will not catch it, so CI stays green. The attempt-log export text is also user-facing (landlord pastes it into records), and its ' — ' separators are the timeline-composition pattern the lens-guard explicitly flags.
recommended_fix: Rephrase the five toasts and the export separators without em-dashes (period + sentence split, as server form_copy does), and extend no_em_dash_test to scan the refcheck_* constants so the ban is pinned.

title: Take-over during a sweep tick: the per-step claim/advance SQL does not re-check taken_over_at, so a row selected before the take-over can still receive its T0 invite/reminder after it
location: server/src/reference_checks/sql/sweep_claim_t0.sql:29-31 (WHERE status='queued' AND attempt_count=0), sweep_advance.sql:22, sweep_due_reference_calls.sql:54 (the only taken_over_at gate); server/src/reference_checks/actions_handler.gleam:52-96 (do_take_over)
evidence: The sweep's send-then-claim flow (sweep.gleam step_t0: send_invite, then sweep_claim_t0) gates the send only on the due-SELECT (sweep_due_reference_calls.sql:54 'AND rc.taken_over_at IS NULL'). If the landlord takes over after the tick's SELECT but before the row's send is dispatched (rows are processed sequentially, each send an HTTP call), the invite still goes out after taken_over_at is set, and the claim UPDATE then succeeds because it does not filter taken_over_at. The take-over handler itself stands down gracefully on its own 0-row guard (409), so this is the reverse direction only.
detail: Narrow window (the row must be queued, selected by an in-flight tick, and not yet processed when the click lands), and the row state stays truthful (the invite did go out; the panel still renders the taken-over surface). But it violates A7's 'the sweep stops sending' and the take-over confirm copy 'Automated messages stop' for that one in-flight message, and the sweep exclusion is only pinned at the SELECT, not at the write steps.
recommended_fix: Re-check taken_over_at IS NULL in sweep_claim_t0/sweep_advance (the claim then 0-rows and the row stays consistent), or re-read the row immediately before dispatching each send.
